forecast_results.prediction: Delivery Hero bridge-to-term-loan conversion is priced <=5.7% weighted-average coupon with no first-time maintenance covenant
forecast_results.evidence: Uber executed a senior unsecured Term Loan Credit Agreement on 2026-08-06 (SEC 8-K ex10-3, TipRanks/StockTitan coverage, accessed 2026-09-08) that DOES include a financial maintenance covenant -- a minimum interest-coverage ratio of at least 3.00-to-1.00, tested on an ongoing basis, alongside limits on additional secured debt and a $500mm cross-default/judgment threshold. The forecast required BOTH conditions (pricing <=5.7% AND no first-time maintenance covenant) to hold; since a maintenance covenant did appear, the conjunctive forecast is falsified regardless of the pricing leg. Margin data found (EURIBOR/ESTR loans priced at a margin of roughly mid-0.x% to ~1.3-1.4% over the reference rate, rating-dependent, per the same 8-K coverage) suggests the ALL-IN coupon is plausibly still below 5.7%, but this was not independently confirmed as a weighted-average figure. This review could not confirm from public sources whether Uber had a prior maintenance covenant in an existing facility, so 'first-time' is treated as most-likely-true based on the pre-mortem's own framing rather than independently re-verified.

The single most consequential development this review found: the forecast this run's own pre-mortem flagged as MORE probable than its headline derivative-lawsuit risk -- a first-ever maintenance covenant appearing in the Delivery Hero financing -- appears to have happened. The 2026-08-06 Term Loan Credit Agreement (executed 3 days before this run's decision_date) discloses a 3.00x minimum interest-coverage covenant. This falsifies the specific conjunctive forecast (pricing<=5.7% AND no maintenance covenant) and is treated as the risk 'trending toward materializing' on the covenant leg -- exactly the direction the pre-mortem anticipated, which is itself informative about this run's own red-team calibration (see pre_mortem_check).

The derivative lawsuit -- the risk this run's OWN headline foregrounded as the killer risk -- remains at an early procedural stage (no MTD filed; case-management conference not until 2026-10-20), consistent with the pre-mortem's argument that it was LESS proximate than the financing-covenant risk. This is a genuinely useful early data point on this run's internal risk-ranking, though far from conclusive at 30 days.

memo_delta.summary: Thirty days into the Watchlist call, UBER is up +11.1% (vs. the S&P 500's -0.5%), and the run's own pre-mortem re-ranking looks directionally supported: the Delivery Hero financing-covenant risk it flagged as MORE proximate than the derivative lawsuit shows a real data point (a 3.00x minimum interest-coverage maintenance covenant disclosed 2026-08-06), while the derivative lawsuit remains at the initial pleadings stage (case-management conference not until 2026-10-20). Nothing has fully resolved either way.
memo_delta.stage_one_comment: Uber is up about 11% since our August 9 Watchlist call, well ahead of a roughly flat-to-down S&P 500, but the two risks we named have moved in different directions. The federal shareholder lawsuit over the board's safety disclosures -- the risk our report's headline focused on -- is still very early: no ruling, not even a formal motion to dismiss yet, with the next real step not until an October 20 court conference. But our own internal red-team review, done right after the report was written, flagged a DIFFERENT risk as more likely to bite first: whether Uber's Delivery Hero financing would come with a real ongoing covenant. It has -- a signed loan agreement from August 6 requires Uber to keep meeting a minimum interest-coverage test, something it apparently has not had to do before. We still cannot say how much cushion Uber has against that test. We are not changing the rating, but this is a real, if partial, confirmation of our own report's internal caution about where the actual risk sits. Next real test: the Q3 earnings print and the October 20 court conference.
